A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the pyrite mining sludge is a source of metal pollution, and that its mobility is increased by oxidation processes, both in the natural and in the laboratory.

(i) the mobility of metals in the initial pyritic sludge is low, excepting the case of copper; (ii) the mobility of several metals in sediments samples of Guadiamár River is high and the levels of metals observed in the zone after the accident are higher than natural values; (iii) the cleaning and inertization works carried out in zone have been insufficient; and (iv) the proposed laboratory ageing procedure can be used for the prediction of the evolution of mobility
the sludge from the Aznalcóllar Mine is not a source of contamination of the Guadiamar River sediments, although the metals levels observed in the Guadiamar are higher than the natural levels.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of accelerated ageing processes in laboratory conditions is a good tool to predict the mobility changes of metals in sludge and sediments.
the mobility of metals is related with their mineralogical association and the degree of oxidation of the pyrite.
the application of a simple laboratory procedure to induce the ageing process of the sludge allows to evaluate the changes in the mobility and therefore the toxicity of the sludge over time.
